statusDetail: Atomic coverage complete across 58 checks and five representative paths.

page.notes: Public Pakistani fashion-commerce storefront with home, listing, product, search, and error templates. Locale/notification overlays appear on first load.

paths.description: Homepage and first-load experience; global navigation, hero, overlays, preferences, performance, security, and crawler behavior. Represents global chrome. Not covering every campaign module because they reuse the same template.
Ready-to-wear collection listing; represents product grids, filtering, scrolling, responsive cards, and repeated interaction. Other collection categories were de-duplicated as the same archetype.
Sample product detail and pre-cart journey; represents product metadata, pricing, sizing, and add-to-bag state. Checkout/payment was not submitted to avoid a real transaction.
Search results for “lawn”; represents search discovery and listing state.
Deliberately invalid URL; represents HTTP/error recovery. Server 500 behavior and offline checkout were not forced against production.

findings.summary: Two unsolicited overlays obscure the primary experience on arrival.
findings.evidence: Desktop and mobile screenshots show a country-switch modal over the page; mobile also shows a notification solicitation above it. The modal occupies most of the 360×800 viewport on home, collection, product, and search paths.
findings.suggestedFix: Do not open either prompt on first paint. Infer locale unobtrusively, offer a dismissible inline switcher, and ask for notifications only after a user action demonstrates intent. Use a named native dialog/popover with light dismiss if an overlay is necessary.

findings.summary: The page does not provide a user-preference-driven dark theme.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-color-scheme: dark, the screenshot remains a light-only interface. The computed root color-scheme is normal, and CSS inspection found only scrollbar-specific dark rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme: light dark and move surface, text, border, form, and overlay colors to tokens using light-dark() or prefers-color-scheme.

findings.summary: Motion continues when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: The reduced-motion probe found three running 1.5-second blinker animations. Some Bootstrap transitions are disabled, but these repeated animations remain active.
findings.suggestedFix: Within prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, stop all non-essential repeated animations and auto-advance, not only framework transitions.

findings.summary: Navigation and adaptive components rely on legacy viewport/global patterns rather than modern declarative primitives.
findings.evidence: Live CSS inspection found no View Transition rules, container queries, CSS anchor positioning, animation-timeline, or scroll-timeline despite route changes, reusable product tiles, menus, and dialogs.
findings.suggestedFix: Adopt View Transitions for route/state changes, container queries for reusable tiles, and anchor positioning for tethered menus where those interactions are next revised; retain fallbacks.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus and touch targeting are not reliably perceivable or usable.
findings.evidence: The focus probe computed outline-style none and no box-shadow on sampled visible controls. Lighthouse failed target-size and identified controls as small as 104×15 CSS px.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator and increase interactive target boxes/spacing to at least 24×24 CSS px, preferably 44×44 for primary touch controls.

findings.summary: The mobile load is slow and ships excessive blocking work.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 6.5 s, TBT 440 ms, Speed Index 9.7 s, and performance 56. The independent trace measured LCP 7.94 s, two long tasks, and 97.76 ms TBT. The HAR captured 162 requests and 8.46 MB transferred.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the hero/LCP image, reduce render-blocking CSS chains, defer non-critical scripts and third parties, split long tasks, and retest under mobile throttling.

findings.summary: Unused and third-party code materially inflates the critical load.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse estimated 447 KiB unused JavaScript and 64 KiB unused CSS. HAR recorded 25 scripts and 92 third-party requests, including 674 KB from Google Tag Manager.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove duplicate tags, load analytics after consent/idle, code-split route features, and purge or defer unused CSS/JavaScript.

findings.summary: Important links and dialogs are not fully exposed to assistive technology.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 84 and failed aria-dialog-name and link-name. It identified the country modal without an accessible name and multiple focusable logo/banner/product links without discernible names. The image audit found 19 images without alt text.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every dialog a valid accessible name, ensure linked images/overlay links expose meaningful names, and provide contextual alt text or empty alt for decorative images.

findings.summary: Heading structure and focus treatment do not support reliable navigation.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed heading-order for H4/H5 jumps; recon found two H1 elements on the home page. Focus probes found no visible CSS outline on sampled controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Use one page-level H1, preserve sequential heading levels, and implement a visible focus order/indicator aligned with reading order.

findings.summary: The viewport configuration restricts user zoom.
findings.evidence: The live viewport meta is width=device-width, initial-scale=1, maximum-scale=1. Lighthouse failed meta-viewport because maximum-scale below 5 prevents magnification.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove maximum-scale and any user-scalable restriction; verify reflow and controls at 200% and 400% zoom.

findings.summary: The page logs a resource error and browser inspector issues.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed errors-in-console because ajax-loader.gif returned 404, failed inspector-issues, and reported five BFCache failure reasons.
findings.suggestedFix: Restore or remove the missing asset, resolve DevTools Issues, and eliminate avoidable BFCache blockers.

findings.summary: Image markup is not consistently sized or semantically complete.
findings.evidence: The image primitive found 38 images without width/height, 19 without alt, 68 without srcset, 15 oversized, and 35 in legacy formats. Lighthouse also failed unsized-images.
findings.suggestedFix: Emit intrinsic width/height or aspect-ratio, responsive srcset/sizes, modern formats, and correct alt semantics from the image component.

findings.summary: Some links and crawler directives are invalid.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse failed crawlable-anchors; recon found an href="javascript:;" cart link. Lighthouse also failed robots.txt, and the file uses non-standard Sitemap2 rather than Sitemap for the product sitemap.
findings.suggestedFix: Use real href destinations or buttons for actions, and replace Sitemap2 with a valid Sitemap directive. Revalidate robots.txt.

findings.summary: Product rich metadata does not describe the product entity.
findings.evidence: On the sampled product URL, JSON-LD types were Organization, ClothingStore, and WebPage, with no Product schema. og:type remained website rather than product, despite visible SKU, price, and availability UI.
findings.suggestedFix: Add Product JSON-LD with offers, currency, availability, canonical URL, images, and SKU; emit product-specific Open Graph fields matching visible content.

findings.summary: Cookie and CSP protections are substantially weaker than the HTTPS transport.
findings.evidence: HTTPS, HSTS, nosniff, and frame-ancestors are present, but CSP contains only frame-ancestors. Cookie audit found 18 flagged cookies, including analytics cookies without Secure, widespread SameSite=None, and several roughly 395–400 day cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a nonce/hash-based CSP covering script/style/connect/img/frame sources, mark all HTTPS cookies Secure, use Lax/Strict unless cross-site use is necessary, and reduce identifiers/lifetimes.

findings.summary: Tracking and third-party collection start before demonstrated user intent.
findings.evidence: Tracker capture found 26 third-party origins and six known tracker domains, including Google/DoubleClick, Facebook, and Mixpanel. HAR attributed 92 requests and 6.51 MB to third parties.
findings.suggestedFix: Create a third-party inventory, remove low-value vendors, gate non-essential tracking behind consent, minimize identifiers, and batch remaining analytics.

findings.summary: Several browser-enforced defensive policies are absent or too weak.
findings.evidence: Headers show no Referrer-Policy or Permissions-Policy. HSTS max-age is only 1800 seconds, and CSP provides clickjacking protection but no script/style XSS policy.
findings.suggestedFix: Set an appropriate Referrer-Policy and least-privilege Permissions-Policy, lengthen HSTS after validation, and expand CSP safely with report-only rollout.

findings.summary: Regional commerce data appears hard-coded rather than locale-aware.
findings.evidence: The site links to PK, UK, US, UAE, and rest-of-world storefronts, but the sampled collection emits literal Rs. price strings and the rendered-script probe found no Intl or Temporal use. html lang is en and dir is omitted.
findings.suggestedFix: Format currency/numbers with Intl.NumberFormat using explicit locale/currency data, set lang/dir for each storefront, and use logical CSS properties so translated/RTL layouts remain sound.

findings.summary: Newsletter input assistance is inconsistent.
findings.evidence: Recon found the first email field has autocomplete=email, while a second visible email input has no name, label, aria-label, or autocomplete token.
findings.suggestedFix: Give every newsletter field a persistent label, stable name, type=email, and autocomplete=email; associate validation/help text programmatically.

findings.summary: The page transfers a disproportionate image and third-party payload.
findings.evidence: HAR captured 8.46 MB total, including 6.51 MB images and 6.51 MB third-party bytes. The image audit found 15 oversized, 68 without srcset, and 21 below-fold images without lazy loading.
findings.suggestedFix: Generate responsive AVIF/WebP sources, correctly prioritize only the LCP image, lazy-load below-fold media, deduplicate repeated image downloads, and enforce per-template byte budgets.

taskList.title: Remove first-load prompt stacking and defer notification/locale asks
Cut LCP, JavaScript, image, and third-party payloads
Restore accessible names, headings, focus, touch targets, and zoom
Harden CSP, cookies, HSTS, Referrer-Policy, and Permissions-Policy
Repair image component semantics and responsive delivery
Fix crawler links/directives and add Product structured data
Add full preference and locale adaptation
Adopt modern declarative interaction primitives during component upgrades
Clear console, DevTools, and BFCache issues
